findings.text: §2 lists `_wait_probe_is_a_no_op` (reckon/crew/recovery_wait.py:803, read at reckon/crew/recovery_liveness.py:965) among the sites that must "read through" the new reader, but that function returns None from `_manifest_wait` — the manifest reads as declaring no wait at all — and today `_wait_probe_is_a_no_op` is False while `_wait_probe_cannot_fail` is True for both `["bash","-c","true"]` and `["python3","-c","true"]` (measured at HEAD 2c79e34857), so a visible "cannot fail" refusal would become a silent drop, the failure the module's own comment at recovery_wait.py:213-218 calls the defect; the two tests inside `_wait_probe_cannot_fail` listed beside it likewise need no change because they already refuse through `_wait_probe_reference_kind`
